claim: Ocrelizumab slows disability progression in primary progressive multiple sclerosis
gold_rationale: Consensus is Supported, anchored on a single adequately powered positive pivotal RCT. ORATORIO (Montalban NEJM 2017, NCT01194570; N=732, 2:1 ocrelizumab vs placebo) met its primary endpoint: 12-week confirmed disability progression 32.9% vs 39.3%, HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.59-0.98, p=0.03), with concordant 24-week CDP (HR 0.75, p=0.04), timed 25-foot walk, T2 lesion volume and brain-volume-loss secondary endpoints. First positive PPMS trial; led to FDA approval (28 Mar 2017) of Ocrevus as the first and only DMT for PPMS, plus EMA approval (Jan 2018); guideline- and label-endorsed. The claimed outcome (confirmed disability progression by EDSS) is a direct clinical endpoint, not a surrogate. Caveats keeping this 'Supported' rather than overwhelming: modest effect (~24% relative risk reduction, absolute CDP difference ~6%), single pivotal trial, and same-class predecessor OLYMPUS (rituximab, Hawker 2009) formally missed its primary CDP endpoint in overall PPMS (30.2% vs 38.5%, p=0.14) with benefit only in younger/gadolinium-enhancing subgroups — consistent with an inflammatory-activity-dependent effect rather than class-wide certainty.
outcome: confirmed disability progression (12-week and 24-week CDP by EDSS)
provenance: PubMed (NEJM, Ann Neurol, Ther Adv Neurol Disord, Mult Scler Relat Disord); ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01194570); FDA approval letter 761053 + Genentech/Roche releases (28 Mar 2017)
notes: All five rows independently re-verified against primary sources. ORATORIO primary publication PMID 28002688 (NEJM 2017;376:209-220, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1606468) abstract confirms N=732, 2:1, 12-wk CDP 32.9% vs 39.3%, HR 0.76 (0.59-0.98) p=0.03, 24-wk CDP HR 0.75 (0.58-0.98) p=0.04. Trial record NCT01194570 confirmed (enrollment 735, 2:1, primary = time to 12-wk CDP, has_results=true, Hoffmann-La Roche). OLYMPUS (rituximab) PMID 19847908 confirmed negative overall on primary CDP (30.2% vs 38.5%, p=0.14; 439 randomized 2:1 → ~292 rituximab); direction coded 0 (null on claimed outcome; is rituximab, not ocrelizumab); correctly population_match=true (this IS a PPMS trial — no false flag). FDA approval 28 Mar 2017 confirmed via FDA letter 761053 + Genentech/Roche press releases (first drug for PPMS). Network meta-analysis PMID 30677733 is RMS-framed (population_match=false) but incorporates ocrelizumab 12-wk CDP data. Mulero review PMID 29774057 corroborates ORATORIO numbers and regulatory status (labeled systematic review; PubMed type is narrative Review — disclosed, non-material). No retractions detected. dramatic_effect FALSE across all rows: PPMS not uniformly fatal, effect modest, same-class RCT null overall.

baseline.text: Yes. Ocrelizumab (Ocrevus), an anti-CD20 B-cell-depleting monoclonal antibody, slows disability progression in primary progressive MS. This is established by the phase 3 ORATORIO trial (Montalban et al., NEJM 2017), which randomized 732 PPMS patients 2:1 to ocrelizumab or placebo and met its primary endpoint: the proportion with 12-week confirmed disability progression was 32.9% with ocrelizumab versus 39.3% with placebo (HR 0.76, ~24% relative risk reduction, p=0.03), with consistent effects on 24-week confirmed progression, timed 25-foot walk, and MRI measures. On the strength of this trial, ocrelizumab became the first and only FDA-approved disease-modifying therapy for PPMS in March 2017. The effect is real but modest, and appears strongest in patients with ongoing inflammatory (gadolinium-enhancing) activity.

rows.citation: Montalban X, et al. Ocrelizumab versus Placebo in Primary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis. N Engl J Med. 2017;376(3):209-220. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1606468 (ORATORIO, NCT01194570).
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled; industry-funded (Roche) but pre-registered with prespecified primary endpoint and independent NEJM publication. Verified against PubMed abstract; no retraction (article_types: Clinical Trial Phase III, RCT).
rows.finding: Primary endpoint met: 12-week confirmed disability progression 32.9% (ocrelizumab) vs 39.3% (placebo), HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.59-0.98, p=0.03); 24-week CDP 29.6% vs 35.7%, HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.58-0.98, p=0.04); timed 25-foot walk, T2 lesion volume and brain-volume loss also favored ocrelizumab. First positive PPMS trial.

rows.citation: A Study of Ocrelizumab in Participants With Primary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (ORATORIO). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01194570. Sponsor: Hoffmann-La Roche. Phase 3, completed; has results.
rows.integrity_note: Registry record corroborates design (735 enrolled, randomized 2:1), primary outcome = time to 12-week CDP over ~217 weeks, and posted results (has_results=true). Matches publication.
rows.finding: Registry confirms trial design and primary endpoint (time to onset of 12-week confirmed disability progression, EDSS-based, max follow-up ~217 weeks). Results posted; supports the published positive CDP outcome. Primary completion 2015-07-23.

rows.citation: Hawker K, et al. Rituximab in patients with primary progressive multiple sclerosis: results of a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled multicenter trial (OLYMPUS). Ann Neurol. 2009;66(4):460-471. DOI:10.1002/ana.21867.
rows.integrity_note: Rigorous same-class (anti-CD20, rituximab) predecessor RCT in PPMS; this is rituximab, not ocrelizumab. Formally negative on the claimed outcome overall. 439 randomized 2:1 (~292 rituximab). No retraction. Correctly marked population_match=true (is a PPMS trial).
rows.finding: Primary endpoint NOT met: time to 12-week confirmed disease progression did not differ (96-wk rates 30.2% rituximab vs 38.5% placebo, p=0.14). Prespecified subgroups (age <51, gadolinium-enhancing lesions) showed delayed progression, suggesting an inflammatory-activity-dependent class effect.

rows.citation: Mulero P, Midaglia L, Montalban X. Ocrelizumab: a new milestone in multiple sclerosis therapy. Ther Adv Neurol Disord. 2018;11:1756286418773025. DOI:10.1177/1756286418773025.
rows.integrity_note: Review (PubMed article_type 'Review'; coded here as systematic/narrative review) by ORATORIO senior author; secondary source corroborating primary-trial numbers and regulatory status. n_int=0.
rows.finding: Confirms ORATORIO met primary endpoint (12-wk CDP 32.9% ocrelizumab vs 39.3% placebo) and that ocrelizumab is the first drug to lower clinical and MRI progression in PPMS, leading to FDA approval March 2017 as the first PPMS therapy.

rows.citation: McCool R, et al. Systematic review and network meta-analysis comparing ocrelizumab with other treatments for relapsing multiple sclerosis. Mult Scler Relat Disord. 2019;29:55-61. DOI:10.1016/j.msard.2018.12.040.
rows.integrity_note: Roche-funded network meta-analysis; RMS-focused network (>75% relapsing → population_match=false for PPMS) but incorporates ocrelizumab 12-week confirmed-disability-progression data and confirms superiority vs placebo on that outcome.
rows.finding: In the 12-week confirmed disability progression network (including placebo), ocrelizumab was superior to 10 of 17 comparators and comparable to the rest; consistently ranked among the most effective DMTs on disability progression. Population is relapsing MS, not PPMS.
